title: EDA verification complexity for billion-transistor designs
bottleneck: Verifying a modern SoC means proving correctness across billions of transistors, multiple clock domains, analog-mixed-signal blocks, and 3D-stacked chiplets; simulation and formal methods scale poorly, and verification now consumes the majority of design effort and schedule. Bugs that escape to silicon cost tens of millions per respin. AI-assisted verification helps but can't yet close the coverage gap.
why_it_blocks: Design cost and risk, not fab cost alone, gate who can build advanced chips: verification complexity prices out all but the largest teams. A single missed bug in an AI accelerator can waste a product generation.
current_state: Commercial EDA flows integrate ML-driven verification, emulation, and formal apps, steadily improving throughput. Complete verification of leading-edge heterogeneous designs remains infeasible in practice.
